conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have two children - Alex, who is 8, and Blake, who is 9.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have two children - Alex (age 8) and Blake (age 9).

Now I need to ask: **Do Alex and Blake live with you in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, yes. Blake lives with me at home, but Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Blake lives with you in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with you.

Let me ask about Alex: **Where does Alex live, and do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives elsewhere - not with me. But yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like clothes, school supplies, and other things Alex needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you contribute towards Alex's upkeep.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex per week or per month, and how regularly do you make these contributions?** 

(For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, and £16.95 per week for additional children.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex. I make these contributions regularly every week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Contributing £30 per week regularly is helpful information.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are both Alex and Blake under 20 years old and not in full-time paid work of 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they're both young - Alex is 8 and Blake is 9, so they're definitely under 20 and not working.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for either Alex or Blake?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, for Blake - the person I live with is already claiming for him. But for Alex, no one where Alex lives is claiming.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. So someone you live with is already claiming Child Benefit for Blake, but no one is claiming for Alex.

Let me ask: **Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This relates to the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, which may apply but doesn't affect eligibility itself.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't have an income over £60,000, no.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.text:
## Your Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment

Based on the information you've provided, here's the outcome for each of your children:

**For Alex (age 8): ELIGIBLE ✓**
Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you are contributing £30 per week regularly towards Alex's upkeep. This exceeds the Child Benefit rate (£25.60 per week for the eldest child). Under the rules, you're considered responsible for a child if you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care. Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you are eligible to claim for Alex.

**For Blake (age 9): INELIGIBLE ✗**
Although Blake lives with you in the UK, someone you live with is already claiming Child Benefit for Blake. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child, so you cannot also claim for Blake while someone else is receiving it for them.

**Summary:** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, but not for Blake due to the existing claim.
